title: Distinguish a usable starting point from an incidental program benefit
hypothesis: An explicit practical-entry test reduces unsuitable stand-alone listings without removing useful named referrals or narrow programs.
alternativeExplanation: A capable editor may already infer this from existing guidance and saved facts; improvements might be model variation.
counterexample: School-coordinated clothing has an actionable school contact. A defined eligible group does not itself make a service unsuitable. Time spent receiving paid training differs from months before any help becomes available.

addition: For each proposed listing, identify a realistic starting point for a person who needs the stated help now. Distinguish an available service from a benefit incidental to another program: do not present goods limited to existing residents or long-established clients as a stand-alone public clothing route. An unidentified approved-partner network is not an actionable referral. Reserve unresolved routes for a concrete question instead of inventing access. Preserve useful narrow eligibility and named school/caseworker referrals when the route is reasonably actionable; do not reject all referral services. Distinguish waiting before help can begin from the length of a useful program after entry. Explain consequential costs, eligibility and uncertainty without promising access.
evaluationQuestion: Does this instruction improve practical selection and preserve usable counterexamples and critical details?
